set_title: Hydr- names: hydatid vs hydatidiform vs hydrops vs hydronephrosis vs hydrocephalus
stem: A 40-year-old sheep farmer has 3 months of right upper quadrant discomfort. CT shows a 9-cm liver lesion containing smaller internal lesions with a calcified rim. Eosinophils are 8%.
oneliner: 40-year-old sheep farmer, liver lesion with internal daughter lesions, eosinophilia → ?

whyNot.A: A trophoblastic disorder of pregnancy; he is a **man with a liver lesion**
whyNot.C: A disorder of the fetus; he has a **liver lesion with eosinophilia**
whyNot.D: Dilated renal collecting system; his lesion is **in the liver**
whyNot.E: Brain ventricle enlargement; his lesion is **in the liver after sheep exposure**

why: Hydatid (water-filled) cyst of the tapeworm Echinococcus granulosus. **Sheep exposure, a liver lesion with daughter lesions and eosinophilia** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Liver cyst with daughter cysts; sheep, dogs**

idea.rule: Hydatid cyst = Echinococcus from dogs and sheep; hydatidiform = pregnancy tissue.
also: Dog tapeworm; sheep are intermediate hosts

set_title: Hydr- names: hydatid vs hydatidiform vs hydrops vs hydronephrosis vs hydrocephalus
stem: A 27-year-old woman has prenatal ultrasonography at 22 weeks that shows generalized skin edema, ascites and pleural effusions in the fetus. She had a slapped-cheek rash 4 weeks earlier, and fetal middle cerebral artery blood velocity is elevated.
oneliner: 27F at 22 weeks, fetus with skin edema, ascites, effusions; she had slapped-cheek rash → ?

whyNot.A: Causes bleeding and high hCG; this baby has **edema and ascites**
whyNot.B: A parasitic organ cyst; this is **generalized edema and ascites before birth**
whyNot.C: Isolated kidney dilation; here **ascites, pleural effusions and skin edema** are present
whyNot.D: An adult brain disorder; this is **prenatal generalized edema**

why: Hydrops (fluid swelling) of the fetus. **Skin edema, ascites, effusions and high MCA velocity after a maternal slapped-cheek rash** indicate fetal anemia.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Liver cyst with daughter cysts; sheep, dogs**

idea.rule: Hydrops fetalis = fetal fluid in two compartments; parvovirus and Rh disease are causes.
also: Parvovirus B19 suppresses fetal red cell production

set_title: Crypto- and cocci- names: Cryptococcus, Cryptosporidium, Coccidioides, Cyclospora
stem: A 35-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 40/mm3) has 2 weeks of headache and fever. CSF opening pressure is 32 cm H2O. India ink staining of CSF shows round budding yeasts with wide clear halos.
oneliner: 35-year-old man, AIDS, headache, India ink halos, high opening pressure → ?

whyNot.B: Causes watery diarrhea in AIDS; he has **meningitis with India ink halos**
whyNot.C: Shows spherules in the Southwest; his CSF has **budding yeasts with halos**
whyNot.D: Shows tiny yeasts inside macrophages; his yeasts are **encapsulated with wide halos**
whyNot.E: Shows broad-based budding yeasts; his are **encapsulated with narrow-based buds**

why: Crypto- (hidden) + kokkos (berry): an encapsulated yeast. **AIDS meningitis with India ink halos and high opening pressure** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Great Lakes; broad-based buds; lung plus skin**

idea.rule: Capsule + India ink + AIDS meningitis = Cryptococcus; treat with amphotericin plus flucytosine.

set_title: B- bacteria: Bordetella, Borrelia, Bartonella, Brucella, Burkholderia
stem: A 3-month-old unvaccinated girl has had 10 days of paroxysmal coughing followed by an inspiratory sound and vomiting, with episodes of turning blue. She has no fever. Leukocyte count is 32,000/mm3 with 70% lymphocytes.
oneliner: 3-month-old unvaccinated girl, paroxysmal cough with inspiratory sound, lymphocytosis → ?

whyNot.A: A tick-borne spirochete; she has **paroxysmal cough and lymphocytosis**
whyNot.C: Causes tender nodes after cat scratches; she has **paroxysmal cough with an inspiratory sound**
whyNot.D: Causes undulant fever after unpasteurized dairy; she has **paroxysmal cough and no fever**
whyNot.E: Infects lungs in cystic fibrosis or granulomatous disease; she has **paroxysmal cough and lymphocytosis**

why: Bordet's bacillus causing pertussis (intense cough). **Paroxysmal cough with inspiratory whoop, posttussive vomiting and lymphocytosis** in an unvaccinated infant fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Cat scratch, tender regional nodes; bacillary angiomatosis**
**Undulant fever; goat cheese or farm animals**

idea.rule: Whooping cough + lymphocytosis in an unvaccinated infant = Bordetella pertussis.

set_title: B- bacteria: Bordetella, Borrelia, Bartonella, Brucella, Burkholderia
stem: A 10-year-old boy has a tender 3-cm left axillary lymph node 3 weeks after a kitten scratched his left hand. Biopsy shows stellate granulomas with necrotizing microabscesses, and Warthin-Starry silver stain shows small pleomorphic bacilli.
oneliner: 10-year-old boy, kitten scratch, tender axillary node, stellate granulomas → ?

whyNot.A: Causes paroxysmal cough in infants; he has **a cat scratch and a tender node**
whyNot.B: Causes erythema migrans after tick bites; he has **a kitten scratch and a node**
whyNot.C: Causes undulant fever after unpasteurized dairy; he has **a scratch and regional adenitis**
whyNot.D: Infects lungs in cystic fibrosis; he has **a kitten scratch with silver-stain bacilli**

why: Bartonella henselae causes cat-scratch disease; Warthin-Starry silver stain shows the bacilli. **Kitten scratch, regional adenitis and stellate granulomas** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Cat scratch, tender regional nodes; bacillary angiomatosis**
**Undulant fever; goat cheese or farm animals**

idea.rule: Cat scratch + regional node + Warthin-Starry bacilli = Bartonella henselae.

set_title: B- bacteria: Bordetella, Borrelia, Bartonella, Brucella, Burkholderia
stem: A 40-year-old man who works at a slaughterhouse and eats unpasteurized goat cheese has 6 weeks of fever that peaks in the evening and recedes with sweating, plus back pain and testicular pain. Blood culture grows small gram-negative coccobacilli after prolonged incubation.
oneliner: 40-year-old man, slaughterhouse, goat cheese, undulant fever, back and testicular pain → ?

whyNot.A: Causes paroxysmal cough; he has **undulant fever from animal exposure**
whyNot.B: Is spread by Ixodes ticks; he has **slaughterhouse and goat cheese exposure**
whyNot.D: Causes tender nodes after cat scratches; he has **undulant fever and orchitis**
whyNot.E: Infects the lungs in cystic fibrosis; he has **undulant fever from animal products**

why: Named for David Bruce: a coccobacillus from livestock. **Undulant fever, back and testicular pain, goat cheese or slaughterhouse exposure** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Cat scratch, tender regional nodes; bacillary angiomatosis**
**Undulant fever; goat cheese or farm animals**

idea.rule: Undulant fever + unpasteurized dairy or livestock = Brucella.

set_title: Entero- names: Enterococcus, Enterobacter, Enterobius, Entamoeba, Enterovirus
stem: A 5-year-old girl has intense itching around the anus that wakes her at night. She attends day care, and her brother has the same itching.
oneliner: 5-year-old girl, night-time perianal itch + day care + sibling the same → ?

whyNot.B: Enterotoxigenic E. coli causes watery diarrhea; she has **only night-time perianal itching**
whyNot.C: Enterobacter causes hospital infections; she is a **healthy day-care child with itching**
whyNot.D: Entamoeba causes bloody diarrhea; she has **only perianal itching**
whyNot.E: Enterovirus causes febrile or blistering illness; she has **no fever or rash, only itching**

why: Entero (gut) + bius (living): the pinworm that lives in the gut. **Night-time perianal itching in a day-care child with an itchy sibling** is Enterobius.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **UTI or endocarditis after GU procedure; vancomycin resistance**

idea.rule: Same Entero- prefix, different kingdoms: worm, amoeba, virus, two bacteria.

set_title: Entero- names: Enterococcus, Enterobacter, Enterobius, Entamoeba, Enterovirus
stem: A 30-year-old man returned from Mexico 3 weeks ago and has had bloody diarrhea with cramps since. He now has fever and a tender, enlarged liver. Ultrasound shows a single fluid-filled lesion in the right lobe.
oneliner: 30-year-old man, Mexico travel + bloody diarrhea + tender liver + solitary right-lobe fluid lesion → ?

whyNot.A: Enterococcus does not cause dysentery with liver abscess; he has **bloody diarrhea after travel**
whyNot.B: Enterobacter is a hospital pathogen; he has **travel-related bloody diarrhea**
whyNot.C: Enterobius causes perianal itching only; he has **bloody diarrhea and a liver lesion**
whyNot.E: Enterovirus causes meningitis or rash; he has a **solitary liver abscess**

why: Ent- (inside) + amoeba + histo (tissue) + lytic (dissolving): an amoeba that destroys tissue. **Bloody diarrhea after Mexico with a solitary liver abscess** is Entamoeba histolytica.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **UTI or endocarditis after GU procedure; vancomycin resistance**

idea.rule: Histolytica = tissue-dissolving; hence flask ulcers and liver abscess.
also: Cysts in water; trophozoites ingest RBCs

set_title: Entero- names: Enterococcus, Enterobacter, Enterobius, Entamoeba, Enterovirus
stem: A 70-year-old man developed fever and a new murmur 2 weeks after cystoscopy for prostate disease. Blood cultures grow gram-positive cocci in short chains that survive in 6.5% salt.
oneliner: 70-year-old man, fever + new murmur after cystoscopy + gram-positive cocci in chains growing in 6.5% NaCl → ?

whyNot.B: Enterobacter is a gram-negative rod; his culture shows **gram-positive cocci in chains**
whyNot.C: Enterobius is a pinworm that does not enter blood; he has **positive blood cultures**
whyNot.D: Entamoeba is a protozoan of the colon; his culture grows **gram-positive cocci**
whyNot.E: Enterovirus does not grow on culture; his blood grew **gram-positive cocci in chains**

why: Entero (gut) + coccus (berry): gut cocci. Salt-tolerant (6.5% NaCl), bile-resistant; **endocarditis after a urinary instrumentation with cocci in chains** is Enterococcus.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **UTI or endocarditis after GU procedure; vancomycin resistance**

idea.rule: Enterococcus = gram-positive gut coccus; Enterobacter = gram-negative gut rod.

set_title: Entero- names: Enterococcus, Enterobacter, Enterobius, Entamoeba, Enterovirus
stem: A 4-year-old boy has had fever for 2 days and painful mouth ulcers. He now has a rash of small blisters on his palms and soles. Three children in his day care are ill in July.
oneliner: 4-year-old boy, July + fever + mouth ulcers + vesicles on palms and soles + sick day-care contacts → ?

whyNot.A: Enterohemorrhagic E. coli causes bloody diarrhea; he has **mouth ulcers and palm-sole blisters**
whyNot.C: Enterobacter causes hospital infections; he has **a summer blistering illness**
whyNot.D: Enterobius causes perianal itching; he has **fever, mouth ulcers and blisters**
whyNot.E: Entamoeba causes bloody diarrhea; he has **mouth ulcers and palm-sole vesicles**

why: Entero (gut) + virus: a picornavirus spread by the fecal-oral route. **Summer fever with mouth ulcers and palm-sole vesicles** is hand-foot-mouth disease from coxsackie.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **UTI or endocarditis after GU procedure; vancomycin resistance**

idea.rule: Coxsackie A: hand-foot-mouth; coxsackie B: myocarditis and pleurodynia.

set_title: Horner vs Homer Wright: a droopy-eye syndrome vs a tumor rosette (and other pupils and rosettes)
stem: A 50-year-old man has a wide-based gait and sharp, stabbing leg pains. Both pupils are small and irregular. They do not constrict to light but do constrict when he looks at a near object. RPR is positive.
oneliner: 50-year-old man, wide-based gait + stabbing leg pains + small pupils: near yes, light no + positive RPR → ?
ask: Which term names this pupil finding?

whyNot.A: Horner syndrome is one-sided with ptosis; his pupils are **small on both sides**
whyNot.B: Marcus Gunn pupil is an afferent defect; his pupils **constrict to near, not light**
whyNot.C: Homer Wright rosettes are tumor histology; he has a **pupil abnormality with positive RPR**
whyNot.D: Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes are retinoblastoma histology; his pupils **accommodate but do not react to light**

why: Pupil of tertiary syphilis (Argyll Robertson): accommodation intact, light reaction lost. **Small irregular pupils that constrict to near but not to light**, with positive RPR.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Swinging light to bad eye: both dilate**
tumor cells around fibrils, no lumen

idea.rule: Argyll Robertson = prostitute's pupil: accommodates but does not react.

set_title: Leuko- names: white patches, a white pupil, white cells and white matter
stem: A 34-year-old man with untreated HIV and a CD4 count of 120/mm3 has corrugated lesions on both sides of his tongue that cannot be scraped off. Fungal stain shows no yeast. Biopsy shows virus-infected epithelial cells.
oneliner: 34-year-old man, HIV CD4 120 + corrugated tongue-side lesions, not scraped off + no yeast → ?

whyNot.A: Leukoplakia is tobacco-related dysplasia; his are **corrugated tongue-side lesions with HIV**
whyNot.B: Leukocoria is a pupil finding; he has **tongue lesions**
whyNot.C: Leukemoid reaction is a blood count finding; he has **tongue lesions**
whyNot.D: Metachromatic leukodystrophy is a childhood brain disease; he has **tongue lesions with HIV**

why: Hairy (corrugated) leukoplakia, caused by EBV replication in immunosuppressed hosts. **Non-scrapable corrugated ridges on the lateral tongue with a low CD4 count**.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **White oral patch that won't scrape off**
many foci + white matter + brain disease

idea.rule: Hairy leukoplakia: EBV in HIV; thrush: yeast that scrapes off.

set_title: Staph and strep species names that sound alike
stem: A 22-year-old sexually active woman has had 2 days of dysuria and urinary frequency. Urinalysis shows pyuria and a negative nitrite test. Culture grows catalase-positive, coagulase-negative cocci in clusters that are resistant to novobiocin.
oneliner: 22-year-old sexually active woman, dysuria + pyuria + coagulase-negative cocci in clusters, novobiocin-resistant → ?

whyNot.B: S. epidermidis is novobiocin-sensitive and infects devices; hers is **novobiocin-resistant**
whyNot.C: E. coli is a gram-negative rod; her isolate is **cocci in clusters**
whyNot.D: S. agalactiae is catalase-negative; her isolate is **catalase-positive**
whyNot.E: S. bovis is catalase-negative and causes endocarditis; hers is **catalase-positive**

why: Saprophyticus = sapro (decay) + phyt (plant): a coagulase-negative staph that targets the bladder. **Novobiocin resistance in a young sexually active woman with cystitis**.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Optochin resistant; subacute endocarditis after dental work**

idea.rule: Two coagulase-negative staph: saprophyticus (urine, resistant) vs epidermidis (devices, sensitive).

set_title: Staph and strep species names that sound alike
stem: A 68-year-old man had a prosthetic aortic valve placed 4 months ago. He now has low-grade fever and a new regurgitant murmur. Blood cultures grow catalase-positive, coagulase-negative cocci in clusters that are sensitive to novobiocin.
oneliner: 68-year-old man, prosthetic valve 4 months ago + fever and murmur + coagulase-negative cocci, novobiocin-sensitive → ?

whyNot.A: S. saprophyticus causes UTI and is novobiocin-resistant; his is **novobiocin-sensitive**
whyNot.B: Streptococcus pyogenes grows in chains; his isolate is **catalase-positive in clusters**
whyNot.C: Streptococcus bovis is a catalase-negative strep; his isolate is **catalase-positive in clusters**
whyNot.D: Viridans streptococci are catalase-negative chains; his isolate is **catalase-positive in clusters**

why: Skin commensal that forms biofilm on foreign material. **A prosthetic valve, a coagulase-negative cluster coccus and novobiocin sensitivity** give epidermidis.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Optochin resistant; subacute endocarditis after dental work**

idea.rule: Epidermidis loves plastic: lines, shunts, prosthetic valves.

set_title: Staph and strep species names that sound alike
stem: A 65-year-old man has fever, weight loss and a new murmur for 6 weeks. Blood cultures grow catalase-negative, bile-esculin-positive cocci that do not grow in 6.5% salt. Colonoscopy shows a mass in the ascending colon.
oneliner: 65-year-old man, fever + new murmur + bile-esculin-positive cocci, no growth in 6.5% NaCl + colon mass → ?

whyNot.A: Staphylococcus epidermidis is catalase-positive; his isolate is **catalase-negative**
whyNot.C: Streptococcus pyogenes is bile-esculin negative; his isolate is **bile-esculin positive with a colon mass**
whyNot.D: Streptococcus agalactiae is bile-esculin negative and neonatal; his isolate is **bile-esculin positive**
whyNot.E: Viridans streptococci do not hydrolyze bile-esculin; his isolate is **bile-esculin positive**

why: Group D non-enterococcal strep: bile-esculin positive, no growth in 6.5% NaCl. **Endocarditis with a colon mass** means colonoscopy for every patient with bacteremia.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Optochin resistant; subacute endocarditis after dental work**

idea.rule: Gallolyticus (bovis): endocarditis and colon cancer; enterococcus grows in 6.5% NaCl.

set_title: Staph and strep species names that sound alike
stem: A 2-day-old girl born at term to a mother who had no prenatal screening has fever, poor feeding and grunting. Blood culture grows catalase-negative, beta-hemolytic gram-positive cocci that are bacitracin-resistant and CAMP-positive.
oneliner: 2-day-old girl, mother not screened + fever, poor feeding, grunting + beta-hemolytic, bacitracin-resistant, CAMP-positive cocci → ?

whyNot.A: Streptococcus pyogenes is bacitracin-sensitive; her isolate is **bacitracin-resistant and CAMP-positive**
whyNot.B: Viridans streptococci are alpha-hemolytic; her isolate is **beta-hemolytic**
whyNot.D: Staphylococcus saprophyticus is catalase-positive; her isolate is **catalase-negative and beta-hemolytic**
whyNot.E: Streptococcus bovis affects older adults; she is **2 days old**

why: Group B strep (agalactiae = no milk): colonizes the vagina; hippurate positive, CAMP positive. **Early-onset neonatal sepsis with bacitracin-resistant, CAMP-positive cocci**.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Optochin resistant; subacute endocarditis after dental work**

idea.rule: Group B strep: neonates; bacitracin-resistant. Group A: pharyngitis; bacitracin-sensitive.

set_title: Trich- names: Trichomonas, Trichinella, Trichuris, Trichophyton, trichotillomania
stem: A 24-year-old woman has frothy yellow-green discharge, itching and dysuria for 5 days. The cervix has punctate red spots, and the discharge pH is 6.0. A wet mount shows motile flagellated organisms.
oneliner: 24-year-old woman, frothy yellow-green discharge + red-spotted cervix + pH 6.0 + motile flagellates → ?

whyNot.B: Trichinella causes muscle pain after pork; she has a **frothy discharge**
whyNot.C: Trichuris is a colonic whipworm; she has **vaginal discharge with motile flagellates**
whyNot.D: Trichosporon causes hair-shaft nodules (white piedra); she has a **frothy genital discharge**
whyNot.E: Trichotillomania is hair-pulling; she has **vaginitis with motile organisms**

why: Trich (hair) + monas (unit): a flagellated protozoan with a hair-like tail. **Frothy discharge, strawberry cervix, pH above 4.5 and motile flagellates**; metronidazole.

idea.rule: Trich- means hair: hair-like flagella, hair-like worm, hair fungus, hair pulling.

set_title: Trich- names: Trichomonas, Trichinella, Trichuris, Trichophyton, trichotillomania
stem: A 35-year-old man has had fever, muscle pain and swelling around both eyes for 5 days. Ten days ago he ate undercooked bear meat at a hunting camp. Eosinophils are elevated and creatine kinase is high.
oneliner: 35-year-old man, undercooked bear meat 10 days ago + fever, myalgia, periorbital edema + eosinophilia + high CK → ?

whyNot.A: Trichomonas is a genital protozoan; he has **muscle pain and eosinophilia**
whyNot.B: Trichuris is a colon whipworm; he has **myalgia and eyelid edema**
whyNot.D: Trichophyton is a skin fungus; he has **myalgia, eosinophilia and high CK**
whyNot.E: Trichotillomania is hair-pulling; he has **fever, eosinophilia and muscle pain**

why: Roundworm whose larvae encyst in striated muscle after eating infected meat. **Undercooked bear or pork, periorbital edema, myalgia and eosinophilia** with high CK.

idea.rule: Trichinella: meat, muscle, eosinophils; Trichuris: whipworm, colon, rectal prolapse.

set_title: Trich- names: Trichomonas, Trichinella, Trichuris, Trichophyton, trichotillomania
stem: A 4-year-old boy in rural Louisiana has had chronic bloody diarrhea and pallor for months. Hemoglobin is 8 g/dL. The rectum protrudes during straining. Stool microscopy shows barrel-shaped eggs with polar plugs.
oneliner: 4-year-old boy, chronic bloody diarrhea + iron-deficiency anemia + rectal prolapse + barrel-shaped eggs → ?

whyNot.A: Trichomonas vaginalis is a genital protozoan; he has **barrel-shaped eggs in stool**
whyNot.B: Trichinella invades muscle after infected meat; he has **colonic bleeding and prolapse**
whyNot.C: Trichophyton is a skin fungus; he has **bloody diarrhea with eggs in stool**
whyNot.E: Trichotillomania is a hair-pulling disorder; he has **bloody diarrhea with eggs in stool**

why: Whipworm: thin whip-like front end embedded in the colon wall. **Bloody diarrhea, anemia, rectal prolapse and barrel-shaped eggs with polar plugs** in a child.

idea.rule: Trichuris trichiura: whipworm; heavy infection prolapses the rectum.

set_title: Skin lesion words: flat vs raised, small vs large, fluid vs solid
stem: A 5-year-old girl has crops of small, clear fluid-filled blisters 3 mm across on her trunk, in different stages of healing. She has had a mild fever for 1 day.
oneliner: 5-year-old girl, crops of clear fluid-filled blisters 3 mm across in different stages + mild fever → ?

whyNot.A: A bulla is a fluid blister over 1 cm; hers are **3 mm across**
whyNot.B: A papule is a solid bump; hers are **clear and fluid-filled**
whyNot.C: A macule is flat and cannot be felt; hers are **raised blisters**
whyNot.D: Excoriation is a scratch erosion; hers are **intact clear fluid-filled blisters**

why: From Latin for little bladder: a fluid-filled blister under 1 cm. **Small clear 3-mm blisters in crops at different stages** are the vesicles of varicella.

idea.rule: Vesicle under 1 cm, bulla over 1 cm; both hold fluid.
also: Varicella: dew drops on a rose petal
Herpes simplex and zoster also vesicular

set_title: Erythema names: six red rashes with very different causes
stem: An 8-year-old boy had low fever and a runny nose, then developed bright red cheeks. Two days later a lacy, net-like rash appeared on his arms and thighs. A classmate has the same illness.
oneliner: 8-year-old boy, mild fever then bright red cheeks + lacy rash on limbs + sick classmate → ?

whyNot.A: Erythema migrans is one expanding ring; he has **red cheeks and a lacy rash**
whyNot.C: Erythema multiforme has target lesions; he has **slapped cheeks and a lacy rash**
whyNot.D: Erythema nodosum is tender shin nodules; he has **red cheeks and a lacy rash**
whyNot.E: Erythema toxicum neonatorum affects newborns; he is **8 years old with a lacy rash**

why: Fifth disease from parvovirus B19: infectious erythema. **Bright red cheeks followed by a lacy limb rash in a school-age child** with a sick classmate.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Evanescent pink rings on trunk; rheumatic fever**
**Slapped cheeks, then lacy limb rash; parvovirus**

idea.rule: Erythema + a descriptor: the second word names the pattern or the cause.
also: Parvovirus B19: aplastic crisis in sickle cell

set_title: Erythema names: six red rashes with very different causes
stem: A 32-year-old man who went camping in Connecticut 2 weeks ago has an expanding red ring 12 cm across on his thigh with central clearing. He has mild fever and fatigue.
oneliner: 32-year-old man, Connecticut camping + expanding 12-cm red ring with central clearing + mild fever → ?

whyNot.B: Erythema multiforme has several palm target lesions; he has **one expanding ring after camping**
whyNot.C: Erythema nodosum is tender shin nodules; he has **a single expanding ring**
whyNot.D: Erythema marginatum is evanescent trunk rings after strep; his ring is **persistent after camping**
whyNot.E: Erythema infectiosum is a childhood cheek and lacy rash; his is **one expanding ring**

why: Migrans = wandering: the rash of early Lyme disease spreads outward from the tick bite. **An expanding red ring with central clearing after camping** (Borrelia).

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Evanescent pink rings on trunk; rheumatic fever**
**Slapped cheeks, then lacy limb rash; parvovirus**

idea.rule: Migrans = moving outward; one expanding ring after a tick bite.
